absent: PID allocation, lookup, and reference counting beyond early init and pidfd resolution.
Full pid namespace creation, cloning, reference lifecycle, and reboot signal delivery effects.
Complete sysctl table definitions and permission semantics beyond the two routed controls.
Profiling buffer allocation, enable and disable controls, and SMP timer setup details.
Full ptrace request dispatch, event reporting, signal injection, and resume paths.
Signal wakeup kinds, job control flag transitions, and stop state machine beyond the routed helpers.

findings.text: Pid namespace sysctl teardown releases the registered table and retires the associated sysctl set, then frees the saved table pointer, with the whole sequence active only when sysctl support is compiled in.

Early pid subsystem setup validates the pid limit against the namespace marker, scales default and minimum pid maximum values by possible cpu count, logs the chosen values, prepares the initial namespace idr, and creates a slab cache for pid objects.

Boot time pid namespace sysctl setup registers sysctls for the initial namespace and treats registration failure as fatal, returning success otherwise, with registration compiled out when sysctl is absent.

Foreign file lookup takes the target exec update lock for reading, requires ptrace access permission and rejects exiting tasks, then normalizes a missing file result to no-such-process when the target is exiting and to bad descriptor otherwise.

Pidfd based descriptor duplication resolves the pid object to its thread, reuses the guarded foreign lookup, then installs the obtained file into the caller with close on exec semantics and releases references.

Pidfd getfd system entry rejects any nonzero flags, rejects an empty pidfd file, resolves the pidfd to a pid object, and delegates to the internal duplication helper with the requested descriptor number.
A dedicated mutex and a slab cache pointer exist for pid namespace cache management, indicating serialized creation or teardown of namespace related caches.
Per-level pid caches are held in an array indexed by namespace level, with one cache pointer per possible nesting depth.

Namespace destruction removes the node from the namespace tree, unregisters sysctls, frees common state, destroys the idr, and defers final release through RCU to drop reference counts and free the slab object; a work handler repeats this while walking parents until the initial namespace and while parent references drop to zero.

Last pid sysctl handler operates on the caller active namespace cursor, requires checkpoint restore capability for writes, presents cursor minus one through a bounded integer vector handler, and on successful write advances the cursor by one.

The last pid control is named ns_last_pid, carries an integer length, uses world writable mode with enforcement inside the handler, and is bounded below by zero with an upper bound tied to the initial namespace pid maximum.

Pid namespace reboot is a no-op for the initial namespace; restart commands select hangup and halt or power off select interrupt for later delivery, then the child reaper is signaled with kill under tasklist protection and the caller exits.
Ancestor relationship holds only when the child level is at least the ancestor level and walking child parents up to that level reaches the ancestor object.

Pid namespace install requires administrative privilege in both the target user namespace and the credential user namespace, requires the new namespace to equal or descend from the active namespace, and on success replaces the for-children namespace reference.

Pid namespace operations expose get and put helpers for active and for-children namespaces, an owner accessor returning the user namespace, a parent accessor that only succeeds when the parent chain passes through the active namespace, and two operation vectors for pid and pid for children plus boot registration of caches, sysctls and tree node.
Virtual memory pid namespace sysctl registration has two build variants, one registering the vm table and one doing nothing, selected by configuration.

Memfd noexec handler resolves the caller active namespace, requires administrative privilege for writes, clamps the effective scope to at least the parent scope, validates through a bounded integer vector handler with parent scope as minimum, and stores the new scope on successful write.
The memfd noexec control is named memfd_noexec, stores an integer scope from the initial namespace, uses mode 0644, and is bounded between zero and two inclusive.
Profiling hit entries pair a program counter value with a hit count, and global profiling state consists of an atomic buffer pointer, a length, a shift, and an enabled mode flag.

Profiling hit accounting only proceeds when the enabled mode matches the event type and a buffer exists, then scales the address relative to kernel text start by the configured shift and adds the hit count when inside the buffer length.
Timer based profiling samples the interrupted instruction pointer from interrupt registers but only when the interrupted context was not user mode.

Profile read exposes first the sample step derived from the shift and then the raw buffer bytes, clipping the request to the available size, handling a partial first word byte by byte, and advancing the file offset by the amount returned.
Profile write optionally accepts a timer multiplier on multiprocessor builds and always clears the buffer, with proc operations binding this write plus the profile read and default seek behavior.
Default profiling timer setup is a weak symbol that reports invalid argument, allowing architectures to override it.
Legacy profiling groups use shift three and size eight, with per-page hit and group counts derived from page size and entry size.

Tracer access to a task requires that current be its ptrace parent and additionally requires either owner dumpable state or tracer capability in the task user namespace, evaluated under RCU protection.

Ptrace virtual memory access pins the target memory descriptor, checks tracer permission, delegates the bounded copy to remote memory access on success, releases the descriptor, and reports zero when no descriptor or no permission exists.

Linking a tracee requires an empty trace entry, then adds it to the new parent traced list, reassigns the parent pointer, and holds a reference to the tracer credentials, with the simple wrapper using current credentials.
Ptrace link establishes parenthood by delegating to the common link helper with current credentials.

A spurious pid is indicated when the exit code encodes an exec stop with trap but the reported message pid differs from the current virtual pid, suggesting the old thread leader was replaced without the exec event being waited.

Freezing a traced task refuses listening jobs, spurious pids and fatal signals, and otherwise sets the frozen flag under signal lock; unfreezing clears that flag under signal lock and if a fatal signal arrived clears traced state and wakes traced waiters.

Attach validation holds the tasklist read lock while confirming the child is traced by current, optionally freezing it, then outside the lock requires the child to be inactive in traced or frozen state unless state checking is skipped.

Ptrace option validation rejects bits outside the allowed mask, and suspend seccomp additionally requires specific build options, administrative privilege, disabled seccomp mode, and no existing suspend flag.

Stop setup on attach sends a privileged stop except for seize, and converts an already stopped task into a trapped stop by installing pending trap flags, clearing stopped state, and waking the stopped state.
Attaching to an already stopped task can expose a transient running state to other threads in the same group racing with wait, even though the attaching thread waits for the transition to traced.

Signal wakeup requires holding the target signal lock, marks signal pending, and requests wakeup in the given state plus interruptible, kicking the target when no waiter was woken to handle races with entering stopped state.

Ptrace attach separates seize from classic attach in flag handling and error codes for unknown options, audits the attempt, rejects kernel threads and same thread group members, serializes credential changes and permission checks, then under tasklist write protection rejects exiting or already traced tasks, links the tracee, arms stop behavior, waits for trap completion, and emits an attach notification.
Trace-me allows an untraced task to make its real parent its tracer after a security check, unless the parent is exiting in which case success is reported but tracing is effectively dropped.

Ptrace detach validates the resume signal number, disables architecture breakpoints, then under tasklist write protection assigns the exit code and unlinks the tracee before emitting a detach notification.
